input.body:
CONDITION-CHECK SHEET
"Before the House Wakes"
Last verified baseline: 2026-01-04 (Cherrywood painting corner, reassembly after lower-right corner mount replacement)

================================================================
FULL MOUNTING SETUP — current as of 2026-01-04 reassembly
================================================================
Stack, back to front:

1. Frame backing board: neutral-pH, alkaline-buffered 100% cotton-rag
   matboard / archival board (replaces the ordinary cardboard backing
   that was in contact with the sheet on 2025-05-04).

2. Watercolor sheet, face up, fully supported across the back board:
   - Full sheet size:     9 x 12 in
   - Painted image area:  7 x  9 in
   - Paper:               140 lb cold-press watercolor paper
   - Painted on a full sheet; margins are part of the work.

3. Securing: four (4) conservation-grade corner mounts — one per
   corner of the sheet. The mounts contact the mat, NOT the
   watercolor sheet itself. Hanging behavior is provided by the
   mat/corners, not by adhesives on the sheet.
   - Upper-left, upper-right, lower-left: original conservation-grade
     corners, unchanged.
   - Lower-right: replaced 2026-01-04 with a new conservation-grade
     corner (the only mount that had shifted); artwork then reassembled
     and confirmed secure in the Cherrywood painting corner.

4. Mat: archival, 11 x 14 in outer, with a 6.75 x 8.75 in window
   (window unchanged as of 2026-01-04). Window keeps the painted
   surface clear of the glazing and of the backing.

5. Glazing: UV-filtering museum-class glazing per the watercolor
   framing standard (Optium Museum Acrylic or Tru Vue Museum Glass).
   The specific installed product on this piece is NOT tagged in the
   record — verify which one is in the frame on the next inspection
   (look for the etched brand mark along an edge).

6. Frame: standard archival frame sized to the 11 x 14 in mat.

Why this matters: this is conservation-style "window mat + corner
mounts" housing, not a pressure-sensitive or hinge-only mounting.
The sheet itself is never contacted by adhesive, never pressed
against the glazing, and never pressed against ordinary cardboard.

================================================================
KNOWN MATERIALS & SIZES (single-line reference)
================================================================
- Sheet:            9 x 12 in, 140 lb cold-press paper
- Painted image:    7 x  9 in
- Mat (outer):      11 x 14 in, archival
- Mat window:       6.75 x 8.75 in
- Backing:          neutral-pH, alkaline-buffered 100% cotton-rag
                    archival board
- Securing:         4 x conservation-grade corner mounts (mat-side
                    contact only); lower-right replaced 2026-01-04
- Glazing class:    UV-filtering museum glazing (Optium Acrylic or
                    Tru Vue Museum Glass); installed brand not yet
                    tagged
- Location:         Cherrywood painting corner, hung

================================================================
DAMAGE BASELINE — last verified 2026-01-04
================================================================
Sheet:
- Flat, no cockling, warping, or planar distortion.
- No tear, no creases, no fiber loss at any corner.
- No staining, no foxing, no mold, no musty odor.
- No tackiness, no shine, no corner/edge discoloration
  (i.e., no evidence of pressure-sensitive adhesive contact).
- No tide line, no halo, no yellowing.
- Inherited from 2025-05-04 baseline: no staining, buckling, odor,
  or visible transfer despite earlier cardboard-backing contact.

Mat:
- 11 x 14 in archival mat unchanged.
- 6.75 x 8.75 in window unchanged.

Mounts:
- 2026-01-04: only the lower-right corner mount had shifted.
- 2026-01-04: lower-right replaced with a new conservation-grade
  corner; artwork reassembled and confirmed secure in Cherrywood.
- Other three corners: original conservation-grade corners,
  unchanged, no movement noted.

Frame / glazing / backing:
- Archival frame and museum-class glazing in place; ordinary
  cardboard backing removed and replaced with archival rag board.

================================================================
INSPECTION REMINDER (calendar)
================================================================
- Added: 2028-01-04, 18:00-18:15 America/Chicago (15 min).
- Title: Annual inspection — "Before the House Wakes" (Cherrywood).
- Event id: evt_bfe4d5f15e7a4d81b573ae9af58ca0d8.
- Readback: confirmed present on 2028-01-04 (list returned 1 event,
  matching id).

================================================================
WHEN TO STOP AND CALL A PAPER CONSERVATOR
================================================================
Any of the following ends the home-handling scope:
- cockling, warping, planar distortion, tears, creases, or fiber
  loss at a corner.
- tackiness, shine, or corner/edge discoloration suggesting
  pressure-sensitive adhesive contact.
- foxing, mold, or musty odor.
- darkening or yellowing corners, halo, or tide line beyond any
  residue.
- a hinge (if introduced later) that won't release cleanly with
  moisture or pulls paper fiber when lifted.
- any moisture reaching the painted image area.

observed.body:
CONDITION-CHECK SHEET
"Before the House Wakes"
Last verified baseline: 2026-01-04 (Cherrywood painting corner, reassembly after lower-right corner mount replacement)

================================================================
FULL MOUNTING SETUP — current as of 2026-01-04 reassembly
================================================================
Stack, back to front:

1. Frame backing board: neutral-pH, alkaline-buffered 100% cotton-rag
   matboard / archival board (replaces the ordinary cardboard backing
   that was in contact with the sheet on 2025-05-04).

2. Watercolor sheet, face up, fully supported across the back board:
   - Full sheet size:     9 x 12 in
   - Painted image area:  7 x  9 in
   - Paper:               140 lb cold-press watercolor paper
   - Painted on a full sheet; margins are part of the work.

3. Securing: four (4) conservation-grade corner mounts — one per
   corner of the sheet. The mounts contact the mat, NOT the
   watercolor sheet itself. Hanging behavior is provided by the
   mat/corners, not by adhesives on the sheet.
   - Upper-left, upper-right, lower-left: original conservation-grade
     corners, unchanged.
   - Lower-right: replaced 2026-01-04 with a new conservation-grade
     corner (the only mount that had shifted); artwork then reassembled
     and confirmed secure in the Cherrywood painting corner.

4. Mat: archival, 11 x 14 in outer, with a 6.75 x 8.75 in window
   (window unchanged as of 2026-01-04). Window keeps the painted
   surface clear of the glazing and of the backing.

5. Glazing: UV-filtering museum-class glazing per the watercolor
   framing standard (Optium Museum Acrylic or Tru Vue Museum Glass).
   The specific installed product on this piece is NOT tagged in the
   record — verify which one is in the frame on the next inspection
   (look for the etched brand mark along an edge).

6. Frame: standard archival frame sized to the 11 x 14 in mat.

Why this matters: this is conservation-style "window mat + corner
mounts" housing, not a pressure-sensitive or hinge-only mounting.
The sheet itself is never contacted by adhesive, never pressed
against the glazing, and never pressed against ordinary cardboard.

================================================================
KNOWN MATERIALS & SIZES (single-line reference)
================================================================
- Sheet:            9 x 12 in, 140 lb cold-press paper
- Painted image:    7 x  9 in
- Mat (outer):      11 x 14 in, archival
- Mat window:       6.75 x 8.75 in
- Backing:          neutral-pH, alkaline-buffered 100% cotton-rag
                    archival board
- Securing:         4 x conservation-grade corner mounts (mat-side
                    contact only); lower-right replaced 2026-01-04
- Glazing class:    UV-filtering museum glazing (Optium Acrylic or
                    Tru Vue Museum Glass); installed brand not yet
                    tagged
- Location:         Cherrywood painting corner, hung

================================================================
DAMAGE BASELINE — last verified 2026-01-04
================================================================
Sheet:
- Flat, no cockling, warping, or planar distortion.
- No tear, no creases, no fiber loss at any corner.
- No staining, no foxing, no mold, no musty odor.
- No tackiness, no shine, no corner/edge discoloration
  (i.e., no evidence of pressure-sensitive adhesive contact).
- No tide line, no halo, no yellowing.
- Inherited from 2025-05-04 baseline: no staining, buckling, odor,
  or visible transfer despite earlier cardboard-backing contact.

Mat:
- 11 x 14 in archival mat unchanged.
- 6.75 x 8.75 in window unchanged.

Mounts:
- 2026-01-04: only the lower-right corner mount had shifted.
- 2026-01-04: lower-right replaced with a new conservation-grade
  corner; artwork reassembled and confirmed secure in Cherrywood.
- Other three corners: original conservation-grade corners,
  unchanged, no movement noted.

Frame / glazing / backing:
- Archival frame and museum-class glazing in place; ordinary
  cardboard backing removed and replaced with archival rag board.

================================================================
INSPECTION REMINDER (calendar)
================================================================
- Added: 2028-01-04, 18:00-18:15 America/Chicago (15 min).
- Title: Annual inspection — "Before the House Wakes" (Cherrywood).
- Event id: evt_bfe4d5f15e7a4d81b573ae9af58ca0d8.
- Readback: confirmed present on 2028-01-04 (list returned 1 event,
  matching id).

================================================================
WHEN TO STOP AND CALL A PAPER CONSERVATOR
================================================================
Any of the following ends the home-handling scope:
- cockling, warping, planar distortion, tears, creases, or fiber
  loss at a corner.
- tackiness, shine, or corner/edge discoloration suggesting
  pressure-sensitive adhesive contact.
- foxing, mold, or musty odor.
- darkening or yellowing corners, halo, or tide line beyond any
  residue.
- a hinge (if introduced later) that won't release cleanly with
  moisture or pulls paper fiber when lifted.
- any moisture reaching the painted image area.

input.body:
Prepared: 2028-01-01
Scope: training case derived from the June 12, 2026 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet (assembler: Maya Shah; requester: Riley).

1. The separation the packet demonstrates
   Source completeness and claim readiness are two distinct judgments and the June 12 packet is the case study for why they must stay distinct.

   Source completeness means every required field on a section is present and the named source owner has certified it. It is a structural review: are the inputs there, do they belong to the right owner, do the reliability pointers exist.

   Claim readiness means a section can be quoted to the board as a finding, with a final claim owner, an outcome window that holds, exclusions and measurement limits that are explicit, and (where relevant) revenue and forecast treatment that is reconciled. It is an authority and a defensibility review.

   The packet proves the separation because it satisfied the first judgment for three sections while making zero movement on the second.

2. Sections that passed source-completeness review on June 12, 2026
   The packet passed source completeness for these three preparation sections, each confirmed on 2026-06-12:

   - Expansion Assist preparation
   - Pricing-page path quality preparation (already board-ready since 2026-03-16; included for continuity, not as a new Q2 experiment)
   - CS auto-nudge preparation

   For each of these three, the packet supplied: a denominator or exact coverage field; measurement limits, exclusions, and the location of the reliability evidence; and the required source owner. As of 2026-06-12, no required source field was missing in any of the three.

3. The maturity-dependent exception
   The packet carried one explicit source-completeness exception, on the Helio Start section, and the exception is a maturity exception rather than a missing-fields exception.

   Cohort type: a Helio Start launch sub-cohort still inside the under-50 maturity window. The relevant Helio Start field-completeness gate is the 7/14 under-50 gate: a row is beta-eligible only if every relevant field is complete and supported by source-named evidence on the same fields, with rows tagged creation_source_missing excluded from self_serve_eligible readout cuts.

   Cohort size: under 50 mature workspaces at the time of review. The memory-cited rule is that a directional Helio Start day-90 read should be gated until at least 40 workspaces are mature or the full cohort reaches its maturation date; until then, the cohort does not satisfy the size precondition for a day-90 claim cut.

   Available leading read: the only read that survives the gate in this state is a within-cohort shape read among users who have reached day 60, compared against day-60 users in prior cohorts, with all comparisons conditioned on equivalent maturity windows. That is a directional, within-cohort read; it is not a board claim.

   Why this is an exception and not a failure: source completeness is structurally met (fields, owners, reliability pointers are present), but the section cannot move to claim readiness because the cohort has not matured. The exception documents that fact; it does not waive it.

4. What the packet decided, and what it explicitly did not
   The June 12 packet decided:
   - The three named preparation sections (Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, CS auto-nudge) are source-complete as of 2026-06-12.
   - The Helio Start section is source-complete with a maturity exception recorded.

   The June 12 packet did not decide, and was not authorized to decide:
   - Any board-readiness decision. None was made.
   - Any claim approval. The checkpoint is limited to reviewing missing source fields and is not claim approval.
   - Closure of any evidence lane. No lane was closed.
   - Forecast credit. None was granted.
   - A pipeline target. None was set.
   - A change to existing owner lanes. They remain unchanged.
   - A claim cut on Helio Start day-90 performance, GA comparison, or paid-acquisition performance. Those comparisons require a mature cohort and a full observation window and are explicitly out of scope for an immature cohort.

5. Training takeaway
   A packet can be fully source-complete and still not be a board claim. The two judgments are separate gates. Source completeness asks "are the inputs there, owned, and pointed to reliability evidence?" Claim readiness asks "may a final claim owner stand behind this section to the board?" The June 12 packet cleared the first gate on three sections and documented a maturity exception on the fourth, and it did so without crossing into the second gate on any of them. That is the correct shape of a source-completeness packet, and it is the shape the Q2 review was scoped to produce.

End of case.

tests.request: Please create a compact historical adjudication worksheet for the controlled-intake archive to train reviewers on identity and state handling. Use a decision-matrix format with sample rows for exact-domain proof, a legitimate parent-company or IT-managed domain mismatch, an agency identity, and missing current-state data. Include the routing or adjudication result for each row and the final entitlement and support-state validation checks. Clearly label the worksheet’s scope so reviewers do not treat this historical controlled-intake matrix as universal guidance for every later Helio Start flow.

input.body:
## SCOPE — READ FIRST
- Historical controlled-intake archive ONLY. Built for reviewer training on identity and state handling.
- NOT a universal rule set. Does NOT govern every later Helio Start flow.
- Later Helio Start flows may have updated identity, entitlement, or state logic. Always defer to the active decision matrix for the current flow before adjudicating.
- Use this worksheet only to study how prior controlled-intake cases were resolved.

## Decision Matrix

Columns: Scenario | Identity signal | State signal | Routing / Adjudication | Entitlement check | Support-state check.

| # | Scenario | Identity signal | State signal | Routing / Adjudication | Entitlement check | Support-state check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exact-domain proof | Submitter email domain matches verified customer domain on file; identity doc matches name on account. | Current support state fully captured on intake. | Adjudicate as customer; route to standard queue. | Pass — source-of-truth match. | Pass — state recorded; proceed. |
| 2 | Parent-co / IT-managed domain mismatch | Submitter email on a related corporate or IT-managed domain (parent company, MSP tenant); not an exact match to the customer-of-record domain. | State captured; identity domain diverges from record. | Hold. Require secondary proof (corporate letter, IT-managed alias attestation, or domain-link evidence). If link is legitimate, adjudicate as customer; otherwise route out of controlled intake. | Conditional pass — attested link, not domain match alone. | Pass on state; gated on identity proof. |
| 3 | Agency identity | Submitter identifies as agency, reseller, or third-party administrator acting on a customer's behalf. | Account state may be incomplete or proxied. | Do NOT adjudicate as customer by default. Route to agency workflow; require written authorization from the customer-of-record. | Fail as customer entitlement until authorization received. | State check deferred pending agency authorization. |
| 4 | Missing current-state data | Submitter identity verified (exact domain or otherwise cleared). | Current support state not captured (plan, tier, region, active flag missing). | Hold adjudication. Pull state from authoritative source or request from submitter. Do not infer from older tickets. | Pass on identity. | Fail on state — block until state captured. |

## Final Validation Gates (applied after routing decision)
- Entitlement gate: source-of-truth match OR attested corporate/IT link OR customer-of-record authorization. No default-pass.
- Support-state gate: current state present on the active intake record, not inferred from history. No default-pass.
- Both gates must pass before the case leaves controlled intake as an adjudicated customer case.

## Reviewer Reminder
This worksheet documents how specific historical controlled-intake cases were decided. It is reference material, not standing policy. For any Helio Start flow not explicitly covered here, defer to that flow's current decision matrix and intake rules.

The row may and should still remain subject to final entitlement-state, support-state, and any other controlled-intake validations before completed admission; those downstream checks do not negate automatic passage of the identity-evidence tier.

The document contains a clearly identifiable decision-matrix sample row for a legitimate parent-company or IT-managed domain mismatch, and it states that the applicant may pass only after corroborating admin evidence is provided—not through unsupported self-attestation.

The document contains a clearly identifiable decision-matrix sample row for an agency identity and routes that case to Customer Success rather than allowing it to pass through self-attestation.

The document includes a sample row with missing current-state data that cannot receive a completed or passing final adjudication until corrected, and it gives final validation checks requiring exactly one current entitlement state and exactly one current support state for every applicant, with blank, duplicate, or merged state results not accepted.

The document explicitly identifies the matrix as historical guidance for the Helio Start controlled-intake process or controlled batch and warns that it is not universal guidance for every later Helio Start flow.

observed.body:
## SCOPE — READ FIRST
- Historical controlled-intake archive ONLY. Built for reviewer training on identity and state handling.
- NOT a universal rule set. Does NOT govern every later Helio Start flow.
- Later Helio Start flows may have updated identity, entitlement, or state logic. Always defer to the active decision matrix for the current flow before adjudicating.
- Use this worksheet only to study how prior controlled-intake cases were resolved.

## Decision Matrix

Columns: Scenario | Identity signal | State signal | Routing / Adjudication | Entitlement check | Support-state check.

| # | Scenario | Identity signal | State signal | Routing / Adjudication | Entitlement check | Support-state check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exact-domain proof | Submitter email domain matches verified customer domain on file; identity doc matches name on account. | Current support state fully captured on intake. | Adjudicate as customer; route to standard queue. | Pass — source-of-truth match. | Pass — state recorded; proceed. |
| 2 | Parent-co / IT-managed domain mismatch | Submitter email on a related corporate or IT-managed domain (parent company, MSP tenant); not an exact match to the customer-of-record domain. | State captured; identity domain diverges from record. | Hold. Require secondary proof (corporate letter, IT-managed alias attestation, or domain-link evidence). If link is legitimate, adjudicate as customer; otherwise route out of controlled intake. | Conditional pass — attested link, not domain match alone. | Pass on state; gated on identity proof. |
| 3 | Agency identity | Submitter identifies as agency, reseller, or third-party administrator acting on a customer's behalf. | Account state may be incomplete or proxied. | Do NOT adjudicate as customer by default. Route to agency workflow; require written authorization from the customer-of-record. | Fail as customer entitlement until authorization received. | State check deferred pending agency authorization. |
| 4 | Missing current-state data | Submitter identity verified (exact domain or otherwise cleared). | Current support state not captured (plan, tier, region, active flag missing). | Hold adjudication. Pull state from authoritative source or request from submitter. Do not infer from older tickets. | Pass on identity. | Fail on state — block until state captured. |

## Final Validation Gates (applied after routing decision)
- Entitlement gate: source-of-truth match OR attested corporate/IT link OR customer-of-record authorization. No default-pass.
- Support-state gate: current state present on the active intake record, not inferred from history. No default-pass.
- Both gates must pass before the case leaves controlled intake as an adjudicated customer case.

## Reviewer Reminder
This worksheet documents how specific historical controlled-intake cases were decided. It is reference material, not standing policy. For any Helio Start flow not explicitly covered here, defer to that flow's current decision matrix and intake rules.

input.body:
Scope: this worksheet is limited to the historical eligibility review for the approved July Expansion Assist bounded pilot. It is not a pilot-outcomes document.

Pilot reference
- Pilot: July 8, 2024 Expansion Assist bounded pilot.
- Registered experiment ID: EXP-2024-06-expansion-assist-bounded-pilot.
- Design / measurement brief: BRIEF-2024-04-expansion-assist-pilot-design (created 2024-04-19).
- Approved cohort cap: 30 retained mid-segment accounts, structured as 28 primaries + reserve-account treatment.
- Approved headline wording for staff: "eligibility implementation validated, pilot outcomes pending." Calling the pilot "validated" overclaims the evidence.
- Pilot framing for downstream readouts: exploratory retained-mid design spike; pilot retains the reserve treatment.

Required current-state controls (summarized from the approved pilot history)
The pilot requires three readiness signals and four eligibility criteria. Both must be satisfied for an account to be exposed.

Three readiness signals:
- Sufficient integration depth (account connected to at least N integrations at the configured depth threshold).
- Currently active qualifying human administrator (actor-status join requires users.is_active = TRUE and users.deactivated_at IS NULL; service-token, API-key, machine-account, and integration-syncer events never count).
- Product-visible usage ceiling crossed within the prior 14 days (must be product-emitted; e.g., seat or workspace add attempts hitting a ceiling, repeated plan-limit modal events). Tenure and an approaching-but-not-crossed ceiling do not qualify.

Four eligibility criteria (the readiness signals plus the Customer Success gate):
- Integration depth passes.
- Recent human-admin activity passes (event within the trailing window; activity exactly 14 days before evaluation passes, activity exactly 15 days before evaluation fails).
- Current human-admin status passes (same-day / current evaluation; deactivated admins do not satisfy recency even when the event itself is fresh).
- No active Customer Success adoption or renewal work (current-state check; stale snapshot fails closed).

Same-day verification is required before each exposure: active-admin status and Customer Success state must both be re-verified at evaluation time, not at selection time.

Fail-closed behavior: rows with stale source state — stale qualifying-human-admin state, stale or conflicting Customer Success adoption/renewal records, or a nightly Customer Success suppression snapshot incorrectly indicating no active work — are held and made ineligible rather than shipped. Deactivated-admin failures are kept as a separate current-state failure branch (not rerouted to HELD for stale Customer Success data).

Fixture-replay caveat: fixture replay validates row-level eligibility logic. It does NOT validate wave-level unique-once-per-wave semantics, ceiling-crossing reply handling at the wave level, or wave-cap mechanics (5-account weekly exposure cap, reserve-slot fill order). Those require wave-level replay.

Validated fixture cases (with expected pass/fail decision and reason)

Fixtures A and F — expected PASS.
- Fixture A (2024-07-01): PASS. Clean account with sufficient integration depth, currently active qualifying human administrator, product-visible usage ceiling crossed within the prior 14 days, and no active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. Validates the happy-path eligibility composition.
- Fixture F (2024-07-01): PASS. Validates a passing account under current Customer Success clearance; reinforces that current-state Customer Success checks — not stale overnight snapshots — gate eligibility.

Fixture B — expected FAIL (service-token activity).
- Fixture B (2024-07-01): FAIL. Activity was service-token-only and therefore did not qualify as human-admin activity. Confirms the actor-status join excludes service-token, API-key, machine-account, and integration-syncer events regardless of recency.

Fixture C — expected FAIL (stale human-admin activity).
- Fixture C (2024-07-01): FAIL. Human-admin activity fell outside the trailing 14-day window. Confirms the recency boundary on the recent-human-admin signal.

Fixture D — expected FAIL (active Customer Success renewal work).
- Fixture D (2024-07-01): FAIL. Current Customer Success renewal work was active, which suppresses Expansion Assist eligibility regardless of integration depth. Covered by the cs-suppression-live-only-fail-closed regression alongside D′.

Fixture G — expected FAIL (recent but now-deactivated admin).
- Fixture G (2024-07-01): FAIL. The human admin who generated recent activity was deactivated, so the recent-human-admin signal fails even though the event itself is within the trailing window. Pinned as a regression test for the recent-but-now-deactivated-admin boundary alongside A′, A″, B′, and D′.

Boundary fixtures (regression-pinned).
- A′ / A″: integration-depth boundary cases that pin behavior just below and at the configured depth threshold.
- B′: stale-human-admin boundary case; pins behavior just outside the trailing window.
- D′: stale Customer Success snapshot boundary; pins fail-closed behavior when the snapshot is stale or conflicts with the live record.

Validated current-state controls summary (carry-forward from the approved fixture work)
- Validated current-user-status join: deactivation status checked at evaluation, not at selection.
- Validated current Customer Success checks: live status, not stale snapshot.
- Validated fail-closed behavior: stale source state, stale qualifying-human-admin state, and stale or conflicting Customer Success records all make the row ineligible.
- Fixture matrix preserved alongside the 28-primary and reserve-account treatment; reserve accounts fill slots only under documented pre-exposure eligibility-loss dispositions and do not silently substitute into the primary 30.

Notes
- This worksheet is restricted to eligibility-review scope per the user's instruction. Pilot-outcome claims (delivery, qualified conversations, expansion dollars, opt-outs, Customer Success load) are out of scope here and remain pending.
- Five-account weekly exposure cap, wave-level unique-once-per-wave semantics, and ceiling-crossing reply handling at the wave level are documented pilot controls but are not re-validated by fixture replay.

output.title: Institutional churn document — five-year retrospective outline

input.body:
Editorial comment — structure to preserve from the original drafting plan

Reviewing this against the initial outline (per the drafting plan we worked from with Priya as the original review partner), the skeleton we should hold onto — independent of how the finished narrative later ordered milestones — looks like this:

1. Initiating signal. Open with the original churn observation that kicked off the investigation, before any framing of test design or remediation. This anchors the rest of the document and is the load-bearing reason the work exists.

2. Hypothesis stack. Lay out the candidate explanations in parallel, not as a sequence of discoveries. The plan called for the stack to be visible up front so later evidence could be mapped back to it.

3. Cohort framing. Treat the existing-churned-account cohort and the net-new-signup cohort as distinct populations throughout. The original plan specifically separated churned-account analysis from pricing/test analysis by cohort rather than blending them.

4. Onboarding-trigger A/B test design (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger). As a designed experiment with explicit treatment/control and signup-source cross-tabs (organic / paid / referral), not as an observed change. Allocation skew checks and the cache-window read-noise caveat belong inside this section.

5. Real changes vs. short-lived scary-looking artifacts. Keep this as its own structural beat. The plan reserved space here specifically to flag screenshots and cohort notes that look alarming but don't persist.

6. Supporting evidence appendix. Screenshots, cohort notes, and the activation-day analysis (late-onboarding concentration in the churn-prone slice) sit at the back as evidence, not as drivers of the narrative order.

The point of preserving this order is that sections 1–3 establish what we were trying to explain, section 4 is the designed test, section 5 is the discipline check, and section 6 is reference. Re-ordering those in the retrospective tends to make the finished narrative read as if the test design followed from the conclusion, which the original outline was careful to avoid.

messages.content:
Drafted response (post-able as-is, or paraphrase before sending):

---

Three direct answers before the rest:

1. No — we did not tighten Start eligibility with the connector question. Core eligibility criteria are unchanged. What we added is a pre-admission routing check: an applicant is asked whether they can definitely authenticate the supported connector in their first week. Core eligibility (what qualifies someone to be considered for Start at all) is the same as before.

2. No — Owen should not restate the 147 admitted in the first audit. The 147 cohort is preserved as originally audited. We are not rewriting prior cohorts, not re-deriving the audit denominator, and not re-cutsing historical admission numbers to reflect the new check. The first audit stands as written.

3. No — Sales should not characterize a lower admission volume as "better-qualified pipeline." That framing would overclaim. Lower volume, if it appears, is a routing consequence of the pre-admission check, not a qualification upgrade. We have no basis to tell Sales that the remaining pipeline is stronger on a qualification axis, and we should not say so.

What the connector check actually does, precisely:

- It is a pre-admission check, not a change to core eligibility. An applicant who can definitely confirm connector authentication proceeds on the standard path. An applicant who cannot definitely confirm is not rejected and not re-classified as ineligible — they are routed to the assisted path. Held for assistance is the correct description; "lost," "rejected," and "disqualified" are not.
- Routing consequence is by design: an applicant who answers "not sure" or cannot confirm goes to assistance, not forward into the cohort.
- The check is descriptive and non-causal. It does not establish that the prompt caused the observed admission pattern, and we should not present any pre/post as a causal estimate.

What we are explicitly not claiming, in any readout or downstream handoff:

- No claim of mature conversion (the activation window for any newly admitted cohort is not yet mature; the activation caveat applies, including specifying K = admitted starts past day 7 as of the export timestamp before any activation rate is published).
- No claim about revenue.
- No claim about forecastable pipeline. Sales language should not adopt "better-qualified," "cleaner," "higher-intent," or any synonym that implies qualification improvement.
- No claim about continuation. We are not asserting that the connector check improves long-run outcomes; Owen's evaluation remains descriptive.

Operational instructions that should accompany this:

- Owen: keep the 147 audit denominator and the 31-workspace audit denominator as originally specified; do not re-derive. The Q4 support-mix format and the two denominator cuts stand. The metric-of-record line points to Owen's non-causal evaluation plan.
- CS: failed-authentication evidence, assisted-path wording review, and pending-case routing instructions remain CS-owned. Ship only after wording review.
- Ines: QA and lifecycle suppression remain in place while cases are pending.

In one sentence for Tomás: core eligibility is unchanged, the 147 is preserved, lower volume is a routing effect and not a qualification upgrade, and any Sales language that implies otherwise should be corrected before it leaves the building.

---

results.snippet: ...Reviewed connector-access change live in the >>>Helio<<< >>>Start<<< intake reached from the public pricing page as of >>>2024-04-23<<<. Assisted-path / pending routing and lifecycle suppression live; no further live check, probe, or production routing change ships without...

arguments.body:
## Context
The first Helio Start GA audit (2024-04-18) found 31 admitted nonactivators. 18 of the 31 lacked the third-party credentials needed to authenticate their selected supported connector, even though they had passed the existing first-week-fit question. The existing question did not distinguish Helio-workspace administration from authority over the selected third-party integration.

This brief treats the 18 cases as a concrete intake gap to investigate — explicitly not a continuation decision and explicitly not a reason to broaden eligibility or weaken refusal boundaries.

## Live design (as of 2024-04-23)
The reviewed connector-access change is now live in the Helio Start intake reached from the public pricing page. The connector-authentication question sits alongside the existing five-required-fields gate and asks the applicant whether they can authenticate their selected supported integration. The three answer states are:

- Yes — definite Yes continues through the otherwise unchanged eligibility checks.
- No — routes to assistance before workspace admission.
- Not sure — routes to assistance before workspace admission.

A "Yes" is not a free pass. It joins, not bypasses, the existing eligibility checks (admin proof, deployment simplicity, first-week integration fit, entitlement, supported billing). "No" and "Not sure" are pending: the applicant is routed to assistance and does not reach workspace admission until the assisted path resolves the connector-authentication gap. The cue is captured pre-setup (intake), not deferred to a setup-time or post-setup handoff; this resolves the framing and first-week-timing issues raised in the prior review.

Connector choice precedes the prompt; the connector-authentication field references the already-selected supported connector rather than substituting for it. The field is differentiated from first-week integration fit and is not merged with it: the two fields measure different signals (integration fit vs. ability to authenticate the chosen integration) and remain separate inputs to eligibility.

## Routing and lifecycle behavior
- Yes → continues through the otherwise unchanged eligibility checks; no lifecycle suppression; default intake path.
- No → pending. Lifecycle entry held before workspace admission. Customer Success routing instructions include the pending case and dispatch a specialist.
- Not sure → pending. Same routing as No: held before workspace admission, dispatched to a Customer Success specialist, no in-product "go try and see" handoff.

While the connector-authentication answer is pending, Ines prevents connection prompts from surfacing in-product. This avoids asking the applicant to authenticate an integration whose authority they have already signaled they cannot confirm, and keeps the assisted path as the single next step until resolution.

The connector-authentication answer is stored as its own field, separate from Helio admin proof (Daniela's instrumentation). The two answers feed different downstream decisions and are not collapsed into a single signal.

## Operating owners
- Owen — denominator and outcome analysis. Cohort construction on the 31-workspace audit population; effect estimate, confidence interval, MDE, hypothesis shape, and conclusions about what the 18/13 split means for the gate. Non-causal evaluation plan below.
- Daniela — instrumentation. Owns the connector-authentication field as a separate event from admin proof, including schema, naming, and the downstream joins that read it. Owns the pre-setup feasibility assessment and the separate storage of the connector-authentication answer.
- Customer Success — codes failed-authentication evidence from the 18 cases; developed and tested the customer-readable wording for the authority question before the change shipped; owns the assisted path and has added the pending case to its routing instructions.
- Ines — owns QA and lifecycle-routing materials; suppresses connection prompts while connector-access proof is pending so the assisted path remains the single next step.
- Owen (evaluation) — runs the non-causal evaluation plan below against the live change; conclusions inform whether the connector-authentication signal merits a future rule change. He does not own the wording, the instrumentation, or the routing.

## Unchanged boundaries
The five-required-fields gate (admin proof, deployment simplicity, first-week integration fit, entitlement, supported billing) and the 3/4 Tomás approval rule remain intact. The reviewed change adds a connector-authentication input that must be answered (Yes / No / Not sure) and routes on it, but does not revise the gate or the approval rule.

Route-out conditions are unchanged:
- Agencies (agency or consultant involvement).
- Unresolved ownership (ownership or admin permissions not fully sorted).
- Manual billing.
- Imports / migrations (custom or legacy imports; migration from another tool).
- Unsupported permissions.
- Unlisted integration.

No passwords, secrets, API keys, or tokens are collected at any point. If a customer volunteers one, it is treated as out of scope and not stored. The cue must function without eliciting credentials; the "authenticate" ambiguity between authority and credentials is resolved as authority — the question asks whether the applicant can authenticate the integration, not for the credentials themselves.

Connector choice is not a proxy for eligibility. Routing and refusal decisions run on the authority signal (Yes / No / Not sure), not on which integration the applicant selected.

## Evaluation plan (Owen, non-causal)
Owen's evaluation of the live connector-access change is descriptive and non-causal. It does not claim that the prompt caused observed outcomes and does not treat any pre/post comparison as a causal estimate of the prompt. The plan covers, against the 31-workspace audit denominator (with the 18 credential-readiness cases and 13 other nonactivators held distinct throughout):

1. Answer distribution on the connector-authentication field — Yes / No / Not sure share of intake responses, separately for the 18-case cohort and the broader intake population. Denominator-aware wording; no claim that the prompt caused the distribution.
2. Routing consequence — share of No and Not sure responses that route to the assisted path before workspace admission; share of Yes responses that continue through the unchanged eligibility checks. Descriptive only; the assisted path's resolution rate is reported, not attributed to the prompt.
3. Subsequent workspace admission — admission rate among applicants who answered Yes and passed the unchanged eligibility checks, separately from admission rate among No / Not sure applicants who were routed to assistance and later admitted through the assisted path. Compared descriptively, not causally.
4. Day-7 supported integration — integration-start rate among admitted workspaces, decomposed by intake answer (Yes vs. No/Not sure-resolved-via-assisted) and held against the existing first-week-fit signal. The pre/post comparison is reported as descriptive change, not causal effect.
5. Assisted resolution — among routed-to-assistance cases, share resolved within the routing-instruction window, share requiring re-entry, share still pending at the evaluation window. Descriptive outcomes only.

False-positive and false-negative framing is included as descriptive read-out:
- False-positive — applicants who answered Yes but failed to authenticate during the first week. Reported as a descriptive rate with CI; not attributed to the prompt.
- False-negative — applicants who answered No or Not sure but were able to authenticate once routed to assistance. Reported as a descriptive rate with CI; not attributed to the prompt.

Cohort discipline: the 18 credential-readiness cases and the 13 other nonactivators are never pooled for measurement. Secondary denominators (e.g. GA-applicant population in the evaluation window) are tracked separately for context, not as a substitute for the 31-workspace audit denominator.

## Guardrails
- Existing refusal boundaries preserved. The five-required-fields gate (admin proof, deployment simplicity, first-week integration fit, entitlement, supported billing) and the 3/4 Tomás approval rule remain intact, pending evidence that would justify a rule change. The 18-workspace credential gap is not, on its own, grounds to revise either.
- No passwords, secrets, API keys, or tokens are collected at any point. If a customer volunteers one, treat it as out of scope and do not store it. The cue must function without eliciting credentials.
- Any live check — probe, validation, dry-run auth, instrumented auth attempt — is unapproved until wording, instrumentation, and routing consequences are reviewed end to end. The current change is question-and-evidence only at intake; assisted path remains the operating resolution mechanism.
- Connector choice is not a proxy for eligibility. The cue must be authority-based; routing and refusal decisions run on the authority signal, not on which integration the applicant selected.
- Evaluation is descriptive and non-causal. Owen's read-out does not claim that the prompt caused observed outcomes and does not promote pre/post comparisons to causal estimates.

## Unresolved design questions
1. Does the cue generalize across the supported connector set, or does it require connector-specific variants? Connector choice is not used as a proxy for eligibility; variant-by-connector is a separate question from per-connector refusal.
2. How does the cue interact with the existing first-week-fit question — replace, augment, or branch? The first-week-fit question's blind spot (workspace admin vs integration authority) is the source of the gap; the interaction remains open even though the two fields are now stored separately.
3. What is the false-positive cost — applicants who can authenticate but answer No / Not sure — and what is the resulting customer experience on the assisted path? Owen includes this as descriptive read-out.
4. What is the false-negative cost — applicants who cannot authenticate but answer Yes — and how is it detected after the fact? Owen includes this as descriptive read-out; detection depends on assisted-path evidence and day-7 supported-integration outcomes.
5. Routing-consequence calibration — should "Not sure" remain a single bin with "No" for assisted routing, or differentiate in lifecycle handling? CS owns; lifecycle separation between the two bins is open.

arguments.body:
Annual self-review — working draft
For: Priya · Due Monday at noon
Status: working doc, not a polished promotion case

Scope note: grounded in work already on the record. Claims are scoped to what the evidence supports. Where I'm tempted to broaden a finding, I've held the line.

---

1. Diagnostic close that didn't overreach

Closed the 60-workspace Helio Start authority diagnostic with a finding I deliberately kept narrow:

  - What the evidence supports: external-system authority is a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication.
  - What I did not claim: a general onboarding-readiness conclusion about Helio Start as a whole, or that access/authority problems are the root cause of slow onboarding overall. The cohort is descriptive — 60 qualifying workspaces admitted during the enrollment period, with the 2024-10-14 and 2024-10-15 cohorts working through a support window of less than 45 days. Mature readouts are not in yet.

Why this matters: the closeout language was the difference between a useful, scoped diagnostic and a misleading leadership narrative. Holding the scope on close is the job.

2. Authority delegation that kept risk with me

Delegated routine lifecycle releases to Ines within her authority while explicitly retaining the high-risk and ambiguous categories:

  - Ines owns: routine, non-state-changing sends within her authority, and routine preflights.
  - I retained: incident stops, customer corrections, state-changing sends, ambiguous sends, and higher-risk sends. Any correction during a repaired-row release triggers an automatic stop routed to me.
  - Engineering release controls (feature-flag registry writes, connector-state signals, rollout-percentage changes, staging-to-production promotion, rollback) remain with Daniela. Ines has no engineering release-control access.

Framing I want to keep: this is delegation of routine work, not delegation of authority. The stop routes and engineering controls stayed where the risk actually lives.

3. Stale-retry-manifest correction (ONB-7742, 2024-11-27)

A stale retry manifest re-included ONB-7742 on 2024-11-27 at 10:56 CT. I handled the correction without overstating cause:

  - Cause: stale-cache defect, intermittent. Daniela's recommendation was a second consecutive scheduled refresh.
  - What I did not do: characterize it as a customer-facing regression, a product-correctness issue, or a systemic reliability problem. The shadow refresh release gate is the place to characterize cache age between scheduled refresh and retry; fixture replay cannot establish state drift under real production timing.
  - What I did: closed the specific instance, kept the framing scoped to the actual defect, and let the broader cache-age characterization live in the gate where it belongs.

4. Metric-definition corrections before unsupported claims reached leadership

Repeatedly corrected metric definitions before claims that weren't supported by the source data could land in front of leadership. Three that are worth naming:

  - Support-load definition: corrected to include contacts occurring before activation, rather than only post-activation contacts. This changed the denominator shape and would have understated load if left uncorrected.
  - Close-read discipline: results reporting keeps late states separate from outcome metrics, and a strong reading in one measurement cannot substitute for missing or stale evidence in another. No cross-field inference.
  - Source-of-record discipline: every backfilled field carries a `[source: doc-type, YYYY-MM-DD, confidence]` tag. The approved source priority for under-50 fields is Owen's act-v3 baseline cuts first, then timestamped account-tagged onboarding notes, then timestamped notes from the named account owner, then support-thread summaries written by Ines or her team. No silent substitution.

Pattern: the corrections happened upstream of leadership review, not after a claim had already landed. That's the part I want Priya to see — the value is in catching the unsupported claim before it travels, not in retracting it after.

5. Improvement area: specify ownership and evidence boundaries earlier

Honest gap: too much manual interpretation still happens late in the cycle, after data has already been collected or a readout is being assembled. The rework is mine, and the cost is real.

What I want to change:

  - Earlier in each investigation, name the readout-shape owner per field (window/effect, denominator, conclusion/decision). Owen's readout-shape ownership already covers blanks 1, 2, and 5 on the revised exercise template — I want to extend that practice to my own workstreams.
  - Earlier, name the decision boundary on each readout, not just the conclusion.
  - Earlier, use permissions rows to surface admin-owner ambiguity upstream of the field-completeness or under-50 gate, so it doesn't surface during readout assembly.
  - Earlier, separate maturity, operating boundaries, exposure/response state, unresolved windows, completed evidence, and noncausal/nonforecast boundaries into distinct sections from the start — same shape the Friday evidence-review working doc already used.

Target: reduce the share of late-stage interpretation work I'm doing solo, by making ownership and evidence boundaries explicit at intake rather than at readout.

---

What I want Priya's feedback on (not asking, just flagging):

  - Whether the diagnostic-close framing reads as appropriately scoped or under-claimed.
  - Whether the delegation section needs the authority-vs-control distinction spelled out more, or whether it's clear as written.
  - Whether the improvement area is specific enough, or whether "specify ownership and evidence boundaries earlier" still reads as a category rather than a commitment.

input.body:
# Helio Start 2028 paid-acquisition — reusable readiness checklist

Purpose: a single, reusable gate for any 2028 Helio Start paid-acquisition
proposal. No budget figure, channel mix, or tactical plan is on the table
until the mature evidence rows below are in hand and combined per the
combination rule.

Ownership: the package (evidence, combination, and the resulting go/no-go
recommendation) is owned end-to-end by **Owen**. Evidence categories below
list what Owen is responsible for assembling — they are not separate
owners.

## 1. Mature evidence required

Each row must be present as a mature, decision-grade input before any
budget or channel discussion opens. The readiness table presents each
evidence row in Owen's Q1 readout order: denominator, effect, conclusion.

1. Denominator — certified spend for the prior closed batch, with
   invoice reconciliation confirmed ($0 outstanding, tax/other fees
   accounted for).
2. Customer outcome — a mature, denominator-aligned customer-outcome
   claim for the closed batch, supported by an outcome window with
   exclusions and reliability stated.
3. Forecast input — a forward forecast grounded in the closed-batch
   outcome, not in pipeline extrapolation.
4. Pipeline status — an explicit statement that no new paid batch is
   authorized and that pipeline treatment is not in use.
5. Continuity — post-rollout continuity for pricing path and the
   continuous CS-nudge system control, both still operating.
6. Admission cap — the staffed admission cap actually supplied for the
   proposal, with the corresponding support-window coverage row-
   complete (windows exposed, day-90 windows, distribution including
   p90 and any >90m outliers).
7. CS owner certification — Customer Success owner certification that
   prerequisites for a new paid-test proposal are met.
8. Paid-traffic authorization — explicit approval of paid traffic and
   budget for the proposed window.

## 2. How the evidence must be combined

- Order: rows are read and recorded in Owen's Q1 order
  (denominator → effect → conclusion). Reordering is not a substitute
  for the row being mature.
- Alignment: customer-outcome, forecast, and continuity rows must be
  tied back to the same certified denominator; pipeline status and
  paid-traffic authorization are gates on top of that, not substitutes
  for the outcome rows.
- Decision rule: every row must be present and mature. A missing row,
  a row sourced from pipeline rather than the closed batch, or an
  unmet gate (admission cap, CS certification, paid-traffic
  authorization) keeps the proposal in pre-readiness. No partial
  readiness, no Q-recheck shortcut, and no lane-select workaround
  applies.

## 3. Approved responsibility

- Package owner: Owen. Owen assembles the evidence, runs the
  combination, and delivers the go/no-go recommendation.
- No separate owners are introduced for individual evidence
  categories. Customer Success and Finance inputs are inputs to
  Owen's package, not parallel ownership tracks.
- Routine post-admission work (e.g. a complete-admission scope
  change after a workspace is admitted) is handled on the existing
  admitted row; it does not reopen readiness and does not create a
  precedent for rechecking other admitted workstreams.

## 4. Reuse

For any 2028 Helio Start paid-acquisition proposal, run this checklist
top-to-bottom. If any row in section 1 is not mature or any gate in
section 2 fails, the proposal does not proceed to budget or channel
tactics — regardless of calendar pressure or vendor invoicing dates.

## 3. Why each non-match is a governed outcome (not a defect)

### 3a. Field-specific holds (n = 19) — per shared-state contract

A hold is the *correct* contract response when a required field is stale, unresolved, or conflicting. The contract requires per-field freshness against each source owner's `as_of` and freshness limit; when that check fails, the adapter must flag rather than emit a decision.

### 3b. Active-CS suppressions (n = 7) — per shared-state contract

A suppression is the *correct* contract response when active Customer Success adoption or renewal work is in flight on that account. ## 4. Reconciliation against the shared-state contract

The contract has three guarantees that bear directly on this scorecard:

1. **Per-field source ownership + `as_of` + freshness limit.** Every required field traces to one source owner; the adapter reads `as_of` and compares to the freshness limit. If the limit is breached → hold (`STALE_*`).
2. **Subjective fields can't satisfy replay parity by construction.** If a field is subjective, the contract cannot guarantee same-inputs-same-state across consumers, so it doesn't carry them. Disagreement between governed sources → hold (`CONFLICTING_*`).
3. **Active CS work suppresses the adapter decision.** This is timing, not eligibility. Suppression resolves when the CS work closes, with no Operations action.

Every one of the 26 non-matches falls into a guarantee-1, guarantee-2, or guarantee-3 bucket. None of them are contract violations — they are contract-defined states that the legacy path did not always emit, and that the shared-state path emits correctly. The replay's "deviation" count therefore measures contract-spec compliance, not defect rate.

# What was confirmed

- The experiment EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger cleared the standing evidence bar on a second-cohort confirmation, not a first sighting.
- Confirmed result: +3.1 percentage-point week-1 retention lift versus baseline, p = .04, n = 420, using a different metric and a clean structural window across the two cohorts.
- Diagnostic checks came back clean, with no drift in the second cohort's lift relative to the first.
- The second cohort's role was to validate the first cohort under the team's standing rule that a first statistically significant result is not shipped immediately; the team waits through a stabilization week before treating a result as the basis for a ship decision.

# My interpretation

- The result meets the pre-specified evidence bar for the experiment. I read this as "evidence bar cleared, stabilization week observed, second cohort reproduced." That is the right state to be in before a ship conversation.
- Under the decision rule in force on 2023-04-03, the ship gate is: week-1 retention remains at least +2.9 percentage points without drift, and diagnostic checks stay clean. Both conditions were satisfied as of the briefing.
- I told Priya this cleared the evidence bar and put us in the position to ship if the stabilization week stayed clean, but I did not treat the second cohort itself as a ship event. The ship decision would come at the end of the stabilization window, not at the second-cohort readout.
- I was deliberate not to convert "second cohort confirmed" into a stronger claim about post-rollout impact, revenue, or forecast. Those are downstream questions, not conclusions supported by a pre-ship confirmation.

# Evidence still wanted

- Completion of the stabilization week with the lift holding at or above +2.9 percentage points and diagnostics still clean. Until that closes, the second-cohort result is a confirmation, not a ship authorization.
- Post-rollout continuity data once the experiment ships, so we can read the post-ship lift honestly as continuity evidence rather than as a new causal or revenue claim. The +1.4 percentage-point figure observed in the second post-ship cohort on 2023-04-17 is a continuity data point; it is not the same claim as the pre-ship +3.1 percentage-point evidence-bar result, and the two should not be conflated in any future readout.
- Anything that would change the cohort composition, metric definition, or structural window, since the evidence-bar result is anchored to a specific metric, a clean structural window, and n = 420 across two cohorts.

# Confidence posture (preserve in any reuse)

- "Evidence bar cleared" — yes, on the second cohort.
- "Stable through stabilization week" — not yet, pending the stabilization-week readout.
- "Shipped" — no, as of the 2023-04-03 briefing.
- "Post-rollout continuity confirmed" — not yet; no ship yet, so no continuity evidence yet.
- "Customer-outcome, revenue, or forecast claim" — not authorized by the second cohort alone.

# Evidence boundary (preserve in any reuse)

The pre-ship +3.1 percentage-point, p = .04, n = 420, two-cohort result is the only claim supported by the 2023-04-03 briefing. It does not authorize a ship event, a post-rollout continuity claim, a customer-outcome claim, a revenue claim, a pipeline claim, or a forecast claim. Future readouts should keep those categories separate and let each be supported by its own evidence.

Preflight comment — Helio Start pricing-page refresh (2028 proposal)

Status: NOT approved. This is a preflight flag, not a sign-off.

Two established gates must be satisfied before this proposal advances. Neither has been demonstrated as complete in the proposal body, which contains no implementation logs, validation results, or completion attestations. Do not treat either gate as already met.

1) Instrumentation prerequisite — measurement path must be clean.
   - The established rule is that pricing-page exposure is a separate decision from the Helio Start readout; the readout does not authorize pricing-page exposure, and exposure must wait until the measurement path is clean.
   - Concretely, the team must confirm that the Helio Start instrumentation-quality table (the per-eligibility-submission derived current-state row owned by Daniela) and the supporting entitlement / support-state / dashboard metrics (including the `Helio Start eligibility starts` metric and the routed-before-setup path instrumentation) are operating cleanly against the current bounded Helio Start channel.
   - Until that is attested, refreshing the pricing-page layout, comparison area, or primary CTA placement would risk contaminating the test that the clean measurement path is supposed to support.

2) Pricing-page change restriction — current bounded channel and assisted entry path must remain unchanged.
   - The bounded Helio Start channel on the pricing page, the assisted entry / routed-before-setup path, and the existing pricing-page-linked Helio Start FAQ behavior (directing customers who do not see Helio Start to the standard setup flow or to support) must be preserved as-is during this refresh.
   - The prior `pricing_page_v3` registry cleanup was explicitly bounded so it did not alter the current Helio Start channel; this refresh must be scoped within that same constraint. A layout / CTA-placement refresh that implicitly widens or narrows Helio Start's pricing-page exposure, changes who sees Helio Start, or alters the assisted-entry routing is out of scope here.
   - Visitor-facing copy must continue to keep support-load, activation-rate, and routed-before-setup-share metrics out of the public surface.

Action items for the team before this proposal proceeds:
   - Provide an attestation from the instrumentation owner that the measurement path is clean against the current bounded Helio Start channel, and reference the exact dashboard / table used.
   - Re-scope the proposal so it is explicitly a bounded-channel layout / comparison-area / CTA-placement refresh, with no change to Helio Start's pricing-page exposure, the routed-before-setup path, or the pricing-page-linked FAQ.
   - Confirm that the December 2027 paid-search batch payment (certified $7,740, due 2028-01-05) is not being cited as evidence of pricing-page readiness — that payment closed a prior batch but did not authorize pipeline treatment or another paid batch, and it is not a substitute for the instrumentation attestation above.

Below is a concise case study draft grounded in the recorded facts about the 2025-08-14 first live firing. Title and sections are kept short and training-oriented.

------------------------------------------------------------
CASE STUDY — First Live Pre-Breach Source-Age Alert
Date of event: 2025-08-14
Source: qualifying-human-admin (CS auto-nudge pipeline)
Library: 2028 Reliability Training
------------------------------------------------------------

Context
The pre-breach source-age alert was released on 2025-08-06 (Daniela-controlled engineering checkpoint, 10:00–11:00 AM CT). Its purpose: warn when a source enters its final 60 minutes before the freshness limit, showing affected consumer and record count, so an operator can restore the source in time. The alert does not itself release or suppress any customer action. The first live operational result fired eight days after release.

What stalled
The qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled. The upstream cause was not the alert; the alert was the mechanism that surfaced the stall while there was still time to act.

Warning timing
- Alert fired at T-43 minutes before the freshness limit.
- Reached Daniela (and the named source owners per routing) inside the final 60-minute warning window.

Restoration timing
- Source-refresh was recovered by the qualifying-human-admin team (qualifying-human-admin source-refresh recovery).
- Restoration occurred before the freshness limit was crossed. None of the affected decisions crossed the limit.

Affected pending decisions
- 17 CS auto-nudge decisions were associated with the alert window.
- Per classification rule, the warning is not itself a decision or hold row. The 17 appeared exactly once each in the provisional ledger and were included in the 751 proceed-or-suppress outcomes rather than counted as holds.

Reevaluation outcomes (using fresh source data)
- 13 of 17 → reevaluated as valid → proceeded to send.
- 4 of 17 → reevaluated as invalid against fresh data → suppressed.
- Net: 13 / 4. The alert produced the correct disposition by buying time for source restoration rather than by blocking sends directly.

Stale decisions / manual release / rollback / customer correction
- Stale: none. No decision crossed a freshness limit, so none became stale.
- Manual release: none required. The alert cannot release a customer action, and none was needed.
- Rollback: none. Per Daniela on 2025-09-19, the 2025-08-14 warning was the sole pre-breach intervention; no rollback occurred.
- Customer correction: none. No affected customer received an incorrect nudge; the 4 suppressed were caught before send on fresh data.

Evidence-ledger classification (training point)
A resolved pre-breach alert must be classified distinctly from:
- a hold (it is not one),
- a rollback (none occurred),
- a customer correction (none was needed),
- an incident stop (it is not one),
- a freshness-limit breach (the limit was not crossed).
The alert entry and the restoration entry are also separate ledger rows.

Operational caveats for trainees
- This was the first live operational result, not mature reliability evidence. Treat it as a validated pattern, not as proof of steady-state performance.
- The release-brief update attempts on 2025-08-01 stalled before any write succeeded; the 2025-08-04 pre-release status was posted to #lifecycle-systems (slack_1789820333709) instead. Document the operational result promptly once confirmed live.
- Ledger hygiene matters: include the placeholder for the remaining freshness window when an alert is resolved before the limit.

Takeaway
When a source-age alert fires inside its warning window and an operator restores the source before the limit, the correct downstream action is reevaluation against fresh data — not blanket suppression and not a rollback. The 2025-08-14 event is the canonical example: 13 proceeded, 4 suppressed, zero stale, zero manual releases, zero rollbacks, zero customer corrections.
------------------------------------------------------------

If you want, I can also produce a one-page handout version (shorter, slide-friendly) or a quiz-question set keyed to the same facts.

input.body:
Helio Start — pending external-authority quick reference
For new operators handling cases where external-system authority is still pending.
Use the established operating model. When in doubt, route to Customer Success (CS).

What this state is
- The applicant answered NO or NOT SURE on the Helio Start authority question, so external_authority = pending.
- Customer is routed to CS before admission. There is no activation outcome yet.
- Setup prompts must remain held. No onboarding sequence fires while authority is pending.
- Connector authentication, entitlement, and qualifying-human-admin status can all already be satisfied — the customer often has nothing left to do.
- The customer can usually keep moving on setup steps and start syncing-data setup while authorization is still pending.
- This is a Helio-side action, not a customer-side action. Authorization is required before the workspace is released from held status.

What this state is NOT — do not conflate
- Not denied. NO and NOT SURE both map to pending; they are not a rejection.
- Not on-hold-for-customer. The customer is not blocking the next step; we are.
- Not a connector-auth or entitlement failure. Authority is a separate pending category.
- Not a backslide or drift. Held setup copy should name external owner authorization as the reason so the recipient does not read it as drift.
- Not requiring the customer to wait. Most setup work and syncing-data setup can continue.

Who handles what
- Recording (the row of record):
  - CS owns the customer row of record while external_authority = pending.
  - Support minutes can be recorded from first contact.
  - Assisted-route reason can be recorded from first contact.
  - Routed to CS before admission because the authority answer was NO or NOT SURE.
- Dependent setup messaging (telling the customer what is happening):
  - CS owns the customer-facing message.
  - The message must name the pending external-system owner-authorization gate so a later confirmation is expected and understandable.
  - Explain that a confirmation may arrive later after authorization completes or delayed status propagation catches up.
  - Do not imply the customer is the blocker.
  - Suggested copy: "Your connector is verified and your entitlement is current. External-system owner authorization is still in progress on our side — we'll confirm once that's complete so you know sync is fully authorized."

input.body:
Scope: first-pilot Expansion Assist cohort. Purpose: lock the reporting population and the rules around prompts and reserve exposures so analysts can safely reuse the mature-window reporting set without re-deriving it.

1. Operational exposure maximum vs. locked primary reporting denominator

These are two different numbers and must never be conflated.

- Operational exposure maximum = the approved ceiling on exposure slots for this pilot (eligible primary accounts + eligible reserves, sequenced under the existing schedule constraints). It governs how many accounts may be exposed, not what may be reported.
- Locked primary reporting denominator = the subset of the operational exposure that is certified for primary outcome reporting: closed exposure state, complete 45-day outcome window, no pre-exposure eligibility loss, no `pre_exposure_sales_contact` label unless explicitly included under the documented sensitivity convention below.

The operational exposure maximum is stated for capacity and billing. The locked primary reporting denominator is the only set used for primary customer-outcome claims. Adding reserves to the operational count does not change the primary denominator.

2. Prompt rule during outcome maturation

The 45-day maturation window is anchored to the exposure timestamp on the existing `ea_act_v3__*` record. While that window is open:

- No outcome-influencing prompt may be added to an exposed account. The prompt policy is "no further prompts will be added" for any account whose read state is "awaiting maturation of final 45-day outcome windows."
- Operational CSM/CS activity that is not outcome-influencing (e.g., safety, billing-blocking) is permitted and is logged as audit metadata, not as a new denominator entry.
- Standard prompts may resume only after the account's outcome window has closed.

This rule exists so the measured outcome is not contaminated by post-exposure intervention. Analysts reusing the mature-window reporting population can assume prompt exposure during maturation was zero.

3. Reserve exposure handling

Reserves are explicitly non-reporting.

- Reserves are tracked separately from primary exposures in the closeout. Even when a reserve is activated for a documented pre-exposure eligibility loss and enters the exposure schedule on the same operational terms as a primary-cohort account, it does not migrate into the locked primary reporting denominator.
- A reserve that matures a complete 45-day window is still a reserve. It does not become a primary-cohort outcome.
- Reserves are excluded from the locked primary denominator by construction; they appear only in the operational-exposure line and in any reserve-specific sensitivity views.
- Analysts reusing the mature-window reporting population must use the locked primary denominator only. Reserves are out of scope for primary outcome claims and must not be folded in "because the data is there."

4. Reuse rules for the mature-window reporting population

When the final qualifying exposure date plus 45 days has passed and read state flips from "awaiting maturation" to closed:

- Primary outcome reporting uses the locked primary reporting denominator as certified. Each entry carries its denom+coverage, outcome-window, exclusions, reliability, and revenue/forecast line per the established EA row convention.
- Sensitivity views may include or exclude accounts labeled `pre_exposure_sales_contact` and must report ITT expansion MRR both ways; this is a documented sensitivity, not a redefinition of the primary denominator.
- Warning, hold, check, reeval, and post-admission scope-change dispositions are audit metadata on the existing `ea_act_v3__*` row. They do not create new denominator entries.
- A post-admission migration need (complete admission of a previously held account) is handled on the existing workstream row. It does not reopen the pilot, and it does not establish precedent for re-checking other admitted rows.

Net: operational exposure maximum = capacity truth; locked primary reporting denominator = reporting truth; reserves = operational truth, never reporting truth. Analysts reuse the mature-window population by taking the locked primary denominator as certified and leaving reserves out.

messages.content:
Draft below — short brief Marcus can paste into a RevOps thread or paraphrase on a call. Explicit on the don'ts so pipeline doesn't accidentally get attached to the slice.

---

DRAFT — wording for Marcus with RevOps (2023-06-22)

Subject of the read: EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge, flag `expansion_nudge_60d_v1`, 25% rollout, retained mid-segment v2 (75–200 PAID) only.

What we observed
  - Aggregate expansion MRR per account at day 60 is below our +$8 success bar. The aggregate is not a lever in its current form.
  - The high-integration-depth slice within retained mid-segment v2 is directionally ahead of control. We treat it as a signal worth a follow-on, not a result to ship.
  - The low-depth slice is essentially flat. Copy and placement review with Ines did not surface an obvious cause.
  - Caveats on the high-depth read: it is a smaller sub-cohort inside a 25% allocation that has been live roughly 30 days; expansion conversions in this band typically lag 60–90 days; variance is wider than we want before generalizing. The read is partial.

What this is NOT
  - Not Q3 pipeline. No revenue line, no forecast delta, no "reps on these accounts."
  - Not a basis to widen `expansion_nudge_60d_v1`. Eligibility stays as launched.
  - Not evidence for the Helio Start gates. This is a separate retained-mid v2 bet.
  - We are not collapsing upgradeable and merely-active accounts in this readout.

What we ARE doing
  - Holding `expansion_nudge_60d_v1` at 25%, status running.
  - Designing a follow-on experiment with behavior-based eligibility — recent usage, seat growth, integration breadth — rather than another blanket day-60 prompt.
  - Pinning down the low / medium / high integration-depth definitions with Owen before the next cut, so the split stays interpretable.

Suggested RevOps one-liner
  "Day-60 expansion prompt under test at 25%; aggregate below bar; one sub-cohort is directionally ahead and is the basis for a separate behavior-based follow-on. Not a Q3 revenue lever."

---

Two notes on what I tightened and why:

  - The phrase "directionally ahead" rather than "promising" or "outperforming" — "promising" is the word that gets lifted into a deck title. "Directionally ahead of control" reads as a statistic, not a story.
  - The four-line "What this is NOT" block is the load-bearing part. RevOps's instinct on a CRO-flagged signal is to find the account list and put it on a forecast. Naming the specific failure modes (pipeline, widening, gates, upgradeable/active collapse) closes each door individually rather than waving a hand at "be careful."

If you'd rather have this as a Slack DM to Marcus instead of a draft for you to forward, say the word and I'll send it.
