messages.content:
Here is the draft, and then notes on the boundaries I drew so you can push back if any are wrong.

DRAFT TO OWEN
--------

Hi Owen —

Quick scope check on Expansion Assist before you go further next week.

WHERE THIS SITS
Expansion Assist is the behavior-triggered concept we're carrying out of EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge. Retained-mid work, post-day-60, and it gets evaluated against a higher bar than the time-based nudge did. The 25% slice stays at its current exposure — nothing in this week's read changes that.

WHAT I WANT NEXT WEEK
A measurement-feasibility read, not a prompt design and not an experiment spec. The question is whether the behavior-based concept is observable in our data at all, and if so at what population shape.

THE CUTS
Yes on the three dimensions you proposed — integration depth, active-admin count, usage-ceiling signals — sliced within retained-mid (75–200 v2) and run as a funnel inside each cell, same shape as the act-v3 baseline (expansion_nudge_sent → upgrade_clicked → expansion_mrr). What I want to learn from each cell:
  - Does a behavior-triggered subset exist at all, and how big is it?
  - Is its funnel distinguishable from the day-60 nudged cohort, or does it look like the same population?
  - Where do the cells thin out — is there a slicing dimension that collapses to noise?

WHAT'S NOT IN SCOPE THIS WEEK
  - No prompt copy. No treatment variant. No holdout design.
  - No ship criteria or rollout recommendation.
  - No redesign of the act-v3 reporting units.

If the cells come back with enough signal to support an experiment, that's a separate conversation — Ines and I own the prompt and the spec, not you.

Same cut-doc shape you've been using. Tuesday EOD works.

NOTES ON THE BOUNDARIES
--------

Three calls I made that you may want to adjust:

1.  "Higher bar than the time-based nudge" is in there, but I did not quantify it. If you want Owen to internalize the bar (vs. just hearing that it exists), say what the bar is — e.g. "needs a cell-level lift we couldn't see in the time-based read" — or tell him you'll define it after this week's cuts. Leaving it vague is fine if you want to keep that conversation for later.

2.  "Usage-ceiling signals" is Owen's own phrase, so I kept it open. If you want it bounded (e.g. seat utilization vs. API rate vs. feature depth), say which one or which ones. Unbounded, he may pull three different definitions and you'll spend Tuesday reconciling them.

3.  Deadline is "Tuesday EOD." If you want Wednesday so you have a day to read before Marcus' weekly, swap it. If you want it earlier to leave room for a Thursday review block with Ines, say so.

One thing I deliberately did not include: any framing of what a behavior trigger looks like in product. That's the prompt-design conversation Owen shouldn't be pulling forward into the cut. If he asks, the answer is "that's for the spec, not this read."

Evidence card — for future Helio Start operating reviews
Authored: 2028-01-01 (annual review snapshot)
Cohort: first fully mature post-check cohort (2024-05-20 intake, reviewed 2024-05-23)
Folder: Helio Start

DENOMINATOR-FIRST READ

Intake volume
- 92 completed applications on the 2024-05-20 connector-access intake check.
- 3 routing groups: pending, assisted, ineligible.

Admitted denominator
- 68 admitted workspaces.
- 15 applicants filtered out for missing or uncertain authority before they could become credential stalls; they do not enter the admitted denominator.

Credential-related nonactivators (the central operational finding)
- Prior admitted-workspace baseline: 18 of 147 = 12.2%.
- Current mature post-check cohort: 3 of 68 = 4.4%.
- Absolute drop: 7.8 percentage points. Relative drop: ~64%.
- Interpretation recorded with the cohort: the check reduced residual credential stalls among admitted workspaces without eliminating them.

Seven-day supported first integration (admitted denominator)
- 59 of 68 activated = 86.8%.
- 9 of 68 = 13.2% did not activate in the seven-day window.
- Of the 9 nonactivators, 3 were credential-related; the remaining 6 were other-cause.

Support volume (separate measure; not an activation outcome)
- 11 support contacts across 8 admitted workspaces.
- This is a support-volume read, not a credential-failure count.

WHAT THIS COHORT DID NOT ESTABLISH (separate from the operational finding)
- Paid conversion, ARR, MRR, revenue performance, or revenue forecasting — none are evidenced by this cohort.
- Paid-traffic readiness — the cohort supported continued use of the intake path within its scope but did not by itself support a decision that Helio Start was ready for paid traffic.
- Mature retention — the 86.8% seven-day supported first-integration figure is a descriptive activation measure, not evidence of mature retention.
- Non-overlap / substitutability with the six validated Helio Start cohorts — no non-overlap relationship had been established as of 2024-05-20; totals should not be combined with or substituted for those cohorts.

REVIEW GUIDANCE
- The operational finding (credential-related stalls fell from 12.2% to 4.4% on the admitted denominator) stands on its own.
- Any longer-horizon business outcome (retention shape, paid conversion, revenue, paid-traffic readiness) must come from a separate, properly bounded evidence pass — not from this cohort.
- Future reviewers should not slide the 4.4% figure into retention, revenue, or paid-traffic arguments.

input.body:
[Historical correction, posted 2028-01-01]

The archived body incorrectly treats Helio Start as a fourth approved board-ready lane and reads the cleared proposal gate as authorization for Q2 forecast treatment. The record as of 2026-03-24 was the following.

Approved lane set and boundaries. Three lanes were approved as board-ready on 2026-03-24 by Tomás Vega, with Owen, Ines, and Daniela confirming the applicable source and limit sections: Expansion Assist (EA), pricing-page path quality (Pricing-path), and system controls / CS auto-nudge. The Jan four-lane packet indexes these three as board-ready plus CS auto-nudge as continuous system-control evidence. Helio Start was excluded from the Q1 2026 board operating-evidence section and retained only for traceability. The "four lanes may be presented together" framing in the archived body does not reflect the 2026-03-24 disposition and should not be cited as approved growth evidence.

Mature Helio Start cohorts available then. As of 2026-03-16, Helio Start had two certified mature cohorts with complete day-90 windows: the 86-workspace mature cohort admitted 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-28, and the 91-workspace mature cohort admitted 2025-10-29 through 2025-11-25. The closed paid cohort of 50 workspaces (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-28) is a separate perimeter and is not a mature cohort. (Note: the exact end dates of the two certified day-90 windows were not recorded in the contemporaneous notes; treat the cohort admission windows above as the available bounds, not as the day-90 close-out dates.)

Why Helio Start was not ready on 2026-03-24. No paid-acquisition test was scheduled through 2026-03-31, and Helio Start had no paid traffic, no approved budget, and no acquisition evidence as of 2026-03-24. On 2026-03-09, the Helio Start proposal was still gated on a complete outcome window before paid-active status could support a mature claim, and Marcus Vail's question about whether the two qualifying mature cohorts should create Q2 forecast credit was resolved against granting forecast credit on 2026-03-24.

Acquisition evidence still absent. No paid traffic, no approved budget, no paid-acquisition test scheduled through quarter-end, and therefore no acquisition-side evidence (no spend, no source attribution, no qualified pipeline from a paid channel) was available to attach to a Q1 board operating claim.

What the proposal gate did and did not authorize. The cleared Helio Start proposal gate authorized the proposal to proceed to its next stage; it did not authorize an approved budget, acquisition claims, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. The 2026-03-24 board disposition is consistent with that scope: approved Q1 operating evidence for EA, Pricing-path, and CS auto-nudge without a Helio Start forecast claim.

This comment is a historical correction and does not reopen any closed workstream.

input.message:
January reminder — Helio Start public self-serve applicant guardrails (current state)

Self-serve stays scoped to applicants who complete eligibility in-product. Anything that falls outside that path is handled explicitly, not silently.

Assistance routing (out of self-serve):
- Unsupported permissions or ownership state
- Manual or unsupported billing
- Migration from another platform
- Importing existing data
- Cases flagged for assisted review during intake
These applicants are sent to the appropriate assisted path; they are not admitted via self-serve and are not represented as self-serve completions.

Ineligible routing:
- Final ineligible route = declined applicants
- These are excluded from any abandoned-intake reminder and are not re-engaged by nurture flows as if still in the funnel.

Unresolved cases (intake started, no final route):
- Eligibility is determined from the final route only, after provisional events resolve.
- Unfinished intakes more than 24 hours old are eligible for the abandoned-intake reminder; ineligible and assisted-route cases are excluded from that reminder by design.
- Cases that don't reach a final route are not downgraded into self-serve guidance.

Reminder scope stays within these guardrails; please flag anything that looks like it would broaden routing or disposition handling beyond the above.

input.body:
Accountable owner: Owen Pham (overall A). Riley retains independent audit and causal-claim authority; routine preparation is bounded-delegated to Owen.

RACI key: R = Responsible, A = Accountable, C = Consulted, I = Informed.

Decision areas covered
1. Eligibility definition (account attributes — seat count, use-case fit, integration depth, admin sophistication). A: Riley. R: Owen. C: Eng on integration depth signals.
2. Product-constraint mapping (deployment shape, connector access, admin complexity). A: Owen. R: Owen. C: Eng.
3. Routing rules (self-serve vs assisted-setup, support handoff, billing exception). A: Owen. R: Owen. C: CS on handoff triggers.
4. Pricing-page & badge executive language. A: Riley. R: Owen. C: CS on assisted-route copy. Bounded phrasing only; no implicit 24/7 availability.
5. CS auto-nudge operating controls (routine). A: Owen. R: Owen. C: Riley on claims language.
6. Expansion Assist boundary check. A: Owen. R: Owen. I: Riley.
7. Activation evidence + ledger (Helio Start). A: Owen. R: Owen. I: Riley.
8. Lifecycle-critical state map (per-state accountable owner). A: Owen. R: Owen. C: Eng per state.
9. Self-attestation engineering issue owner (routes back to Owen when model selected). A: Owen. R: Owen. C: Eng.
10. Lifecycle-and-support fork-risk track (downstream + support handoff). A: Owen. R: Owen. C: CS.

Core operating outcomes — weighting
- Mature-activator day-30 retention is the lead outcome. It is the proximate measure of whether self-serve is producing durable, qualified usage; regressions here are treated as a signal that the funnel is selecting rather than the model working.
- Day-14 activation rate is the diagnostic, supporting outcome. It is reported separately from retention and is read as a leading indicator of selection vs. causal effect, not as the primary success metric.

In trade-offs, retention wins. A clean retention number with a soft activation dip is preferred over activation held up by retention being propped by selection.

Reporting discipline (carried forward)
- Activation-v3 and day-30 retention remain separate metrics; no causal claim about activation-v3's effect on retention is made from cohort comparison alone.
- Executive-language copy stays bounded; CS-nudge wording keeps precise messaging-state discipline.
- Closed batches do not authorize forecast credit or pipeline treatment; payment does not by itself support mature customer-outcome claims.

input.body:
Scope. This document reviews the seven mature workspaces from the 2026 Helio Start fixed paid-pilot cohort that exceeded 90 account-level support minutes. It is descriptive of the cohort's cause-classification profile and the rulings-out already established at the certified-mature cohort level; it does not introduce new case-level claims beyond what is in the supporting record.

Cohort and threshold. The fixed paid-cohort contained 50 workspaces. As of 2026-11-13, seven of those 50 had exceeded 90 support minutes, a 14% rate that exceeds the more-than-10% pause threshold that applies once at least 20 workspaces have been admitted. The seven-workspace population is the focus of this review.

Four cause-classification lanes. The Q4 Lifecycle Systems case-review gate sorts high-support cases into four lanes: external-authority action, ordinary integration, supported-billing, and other supported. The first two lanes are the ones most often confused and are the subject of the distinction below.

Distinguishing external owner-permission or network-allowlist coordination from ordinary integration troubleshooting. External owner-permission and network-allowlist cases are classified as the external-authority lane. They share three properties that ordinary integration cases do not:

  - The required action is an out-of-band step performed by the account's connection owner or another identified owner (for example, an AWS organization owner who controls network-allowlist approval). Helio does not perform the connector's required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action on the customer's behalf.
  - Verification is by external-authority status, not by connector behavior. Workspace state is gated on the account or an available owner being able to complete the connector's required permission or network-allowlist step.
  - Reporting is separate. Customer Success requires owner-level permission cases and network-allowlist cases to be reported separately from ordinary Helio Start integration troubleshooting, so that pause-threshold, median, and p90 readings are not skewed by coordination latency.

Ordinary integration troubleshooting, by contrast, stays inside Helio's hands and inside the workspace, and it is the lane that the connector-checklist wording (finalized 2026-10-16) presupposes: "Before setup, confirm that you or an available owner can complete the connector's required permission or network-allowlist step." Once that gate is satisfied, residual time is treated as ordinary integration effort, not as external coordination.

What this means for the seven. The seven workspaces sit inside the same cohort where, on 2026-09-15, 8 of 24 Helio Start replay cases had a selected connector requiring an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action with current verified-yes external authority, and where all 13 Helio Start workspaces with such a connector also had current verified-yes external authority. Across the seven high-support workspaces, the review must therefore identify each case's lane explicitly: external-authority (owner-permission or network-allowlist coordination), ordinary integration, supported-billing, or other supported. Mixed cases are split, not collapsed.

Causes ruled out across all seven cases. At the certified-mature cohort level, two causes are ruled out for the entire 2026 Helio Start admitted path:

  - Unsupported applicants. No unsupported case entered the admitted Helio Start path in the mature cohorts certified on 2026-01-27 and 2026-02-24. The high-support population is therefore not the result of an admission-gate failure on the eligibility side.
  - Manual-billing misclassification at admission. No manual-billing case entered the admitted Helio Start path in the certified mature cohort reported on 2025-12-02, and the 2026-02-24 mature cohort held its billing-hold subset (4 workspaces) outside the cause profile of the seven high-support cases. Supported-billing effort is recognized as its own lane but is not the underlying driver of high-support time across the seven.

The two remaining lanes, external-authority coordination and ordinary integration troubleshooting, are the lanes in which the seven's per-case cause attribution actually lives.

Implications for admission correctness. Admission correctness is intact at the gate level. The admission criteria (external authority, connector authentication, entitlement, QHA, CS-work, per the Q2 2026 paid-acquisition draft's five-field gate) did not let an unsupported or wrongly-billed workspace into the admitted path, and the high-support cases are not evidence of a broken gate. They are evidence of effort within the gate, concentrated in the seven workspaces and weighted toward the lanes where the customer side (owner-permission, network-allowlist) drives time, not toward gate-failure modes. An AWS organization owner who controls network-allowlist approval should be treated as a standing external-authority dependency for future connector changes, scope expansions, and tenant reconfigurations, not as a one-off guidance issue; this reinforces, rather than weakens, the correctness of admitting workspaces whose external authority is current verified-yes.

Operational follow-up.

  - Per-case lane assignment. Each of the seven workspaces gets an explicit lane tag (external-authority / ordinary integration / supported-billing / other supported), with split tagging where a case crosses lanes. Reporting keeps external-authority and ordinary-integration effort in separate columns.
  - Threshold response. Because 14% exceeds the 10% pause threshold, the operational response is governed by the existing pilot rule; this review does not authorize a continuation decision on its own and does not authorize another paid batch.
  - Reporting hygiene. Owner-level permission and network-allowlist cases continue to be reported separately from ordinary integration troubleshooting, so that pause-threshold, median, and p90 readings remain comparable to prior cuts.
  - Standing-lane treatment. Owner-side coordination dependencies (AWS organization owners controlling network-allowlist approval, identified owners for connector permission grants) are tracked as standing external-authority dependencies on the affected workspaces, not as one-off guidance issues.
  - No Q-recheck from this document. This review consolidates cohort-level rulings-out and lane structure; it does not re-open admission decisions on already-admitted workspaces and does not authorize routine preparation beyond what the existing case-review gate already prescribes.

Source notes. Cohort figures are drawn from the 2026-11-13 fixed paid-cohort cut (7 of 50 workspaces above 90 support minutes) and the 2026-09-15 replay cut (8 of 24 with verified-yes external authority on a connector requiring owner-permission or network-allowlist). The four-lane classification follows the Q4 Lifecycle Systems case-review gate. The connector-checklist wording is the 2026-10-16 finalized version. Rulings-out are drawn from the 2026-01-27, 2026-02-24, and 2025-12-02 certified-mature cohort statements.

  explicit approval.
